# Usability study protocol (needed for Section IV-D - this part cannot be generated by code)

The old 5/5 and 3/5 results belong to whichever build those users tried. If they did not use THIS version, run a new session.

**Participants:** 10-15 people (more than 5), not only your classmates if possible. Record n honestly.

**Tasks (each timed, unaided; note any help given):**
1. Sign up and do one mood check-in (mood + occasion).
2. Add 3 wardrobe items and press "Style my mood". Accept or reject the outfit.
3. Add 3 grocery items and find a recipe. Reject one.
4. Add 2 tasks, complete one, open the Task agent insights line.
5. Change the mood and observe what changes. Ask: "Which screens changed after you chose the mood?"

**Measure per participant:** task completed unaided (yes/no), time per task, errors, and the 5-point ratings below.

**Questions (1-5):** The suggestions matched my mood. Entering the mood once was enough. I understood why an outfit/recipe was suggested. I would use this daily.

**Open question:** What did you expect the mood to change that it did not?

**Report:** n, completion counts (x/n), median time, mean ratings with the range. With n < 30 say "indicative only, no inference".
Compare against nothing - this study measures usability, NOT whether the shared mood is better (that is the simulation's job; a real A/B test is future work).
